newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: BSE-hit Dutch farmers to get EU compensation.
newsitem.headline: BSE-hit Dutch farmers to get EU compensation.

text.p: Dutch farmers hit by fallout from the mad cow disease crisis in 1996 will get 63 million guilders ($33 million) in European Union compensation, the Dutch agriculture ministry said on Thursday.

The EU decided in July last year to help farmers who suffered loss of income due to market disturbances from the Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy (BSE) scare and had set aside 70 million guilders for those in the Netherlands, it said.
Seven million will be used to further strengthen monitoring procedures in livestock production, with the rest to flow to affected farmers.

The Dutch last week reported their first domestic case of BSE. In 1996 the country ordered the precautionary slaughter and incineration of 64,000 calves imported from Britain, where the vast majority of cases have been identified.
